entry.title: A non-Golod ring with a trivial product on its Koszul homology
entry.summary: We present a monomial ideal $\mathfrak{a} \subset S$ such that $S/\mathfrak{a}$ is not Golod, even though the product on its Koszul homology is trivial. This constitutes a counterexample to a well-known result by Berglund and Jöllenbeck (the error can be traced to a mistake in an earlier article by Jöllenbeck). On the positive side, we show that if $R$ is a monomial ring such that the $r$-ary Massey product vanish for all $r \leq \max(2, \mathrm{reg} R-2)$, then $R$ is Golod. In particular, if $R$ is the Stanley-Reisner ring of a simplicial complex of dimension at most $3$, then $R$ is Golod if and only if the product on its Koszul homology is trivial. Moreover, we show that if $Δ$ is a triangulation of a $\Bbbk$-orientable manifold whose Stanley-Reisner ring is Golod, then $Δ$ is $2$-neighborly. This extends a recent result of Iriye and Kishimoto.
entry.arxiv:comment: 17 pages, simplified the main example and improved exposition

entry.title: The Golod property for Stanley-Reisner rings in varying characteristic
entry.summary: We show that the Golod property of a Stanley-Reisner ring can depend on the characteristic of the base field. More precisely, for every finite set $T$ of prime numbers we construct simplicial complexes $Δ$ and $Γ$, such that $\mathbb{K}[Δ]$ is Golod exactly in the characteristics in $T$ and $\mathbb{K}[Γ]$ is Golod exactly in the characteristics not in $T$. Along the way, we show that a one-dimensional simplicial complex is Golod if and only if it is chordal.
entry.arxiv:comment: 13 pages. Minor corrections, one simplified proof. To appear in J. Pure and applied Alg
entry.arxiv:journal_ref: Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra, 220(6), 2265-2276 (2016)
